summary: Hormuz blockade after Feb-Mar 2026 war: maritime traffic -97%; PE ~1,176 USD/t and PP ~1,288 USD/t; packaging, agriculture film and auto parts in Algeria hit
implication: At 133 DZD/USD official this is ~171 DZD/kg before duty/margin; at ~240 parallel ~309 DZD/kg. Budget resin at crisis level.

summary: PET +60% to ~1,850 USD/t early April 2026; in Europe PP rose from ~1,300 to ~2,500 EUR/t Feb->Apr 2026 (~+90%); fears PET could hit 3,000 USD/t if blockade lasted 3 months
source_type: news (Maghreb Emergent / French trade press, via snippet)
implication: European-origin PP at 2,500 EUR/t x 155 = ~390 DZD/kg CIF before duty: EU is not a cheap fallback during Gulf disruption.

summary: Algerian transformers face rising prices signalling an approaching raw-material supply crisis; Algeria exports naphtha and methanol but cannot supply its SMEs with resins/granules
implication: Hold 1-2 months of PP/HDPE safety stock; lock supplier relationships before launch.

summary: PE +37% and PP +38% on world markets after war; Hormuz transits down >70%; Algeria plastics (materials+products) imports ~2.98 bn USD in 2025; raw plastic imports grew 7.8%/yr 2007-2024
implication: Confirms 2026 shock reached Algerian discourse; magnitude ~+40% vs 2025.

summary: Algeria imported ~2.98 bn USD of plastic raw materials and products in 2025, +6.8% vs 2024; agrifood packaging depends almost entirely on imported granules
implication: Large, growing converter base = deep distributor market; but 100% import exposure.

summary: French packaging federation Elipso denounced 'abusive force majeure' declarations by resin suppliers using the Hormuz blockade as pretext
implication: Allocation/force majeure risk flows down to Algerian distributors; ask for written price validity.

summary: Counter-signal: European plastics production 'running flat out', risk of shortages in plasturgy expected to stay limited
implication: Availability (at a price) likely; shortage is mainly a price problem for Europe-sourced material.

summary: Government accelerating petrochemical strategy with ~7 bn USD portfolio (naphtha/LPG-based); Arzew PP 550 kt/y launched Sept 2024, completion planned 2027
implication: Policy tailwind for local inputs, but no local PP for a 2026-27 startup.

summary: Arzew PDH-PP stalled: work stopped, Petrofac/HQCEC/STEP talks dragging, end-2026 target out of reach, no restart date
implication: Conflicts with 2027 completion claim; assume first local PP >=2028.

summary: Sonatrach 2024 annual report: CP2K Skikda produced 34,198 t HDPE in 2024 (+101% y/y) vs 130 kt/y nameplate (~26% utilisation)
implication: Local HDPE exists but is small, likely pipe/film grades; ask distributors whether they resell Sonatrach HDPE.

summary: CP2K capacities 'largely insufficient', installations aging, recurrent shutdowns of old local steam cracker
implication: Do not rely on local HDPE continuity.

summary: Raw plastic prices rose >300%, from 170 to 520 DA/kg; many plants and workshops stopped for months for lack of raw material; importers then received licences, imports expected in 30-45 days
implication: Shortage history: Algerian shortages are often policy-driven (import licences), not only global. Pre-crisis baseline ~170 DA/kg.

summary: Recycled plastic price rose from 100 to 250 DA/kg during the same crisis
implication: Regrind tracks virgin price in shortages; not a full hedge.

summary: Plastic waste: 15-20 DA/kg from associations, 30-50 DA/kg from industrial firms/traders; clean PEHD waste 25-35 DA/kg
implication: Feedstock cheap; value added by washing/grinding/granulating. Supports in-house regrind and buying broyé.

summary: Listing: industrial-origin transparent PEHD extrusion broyé at 110,000 DA/t (110 DA/kg)
implication: Regrind roughly 40-60% of estimated virgin price; extrusion grade (low MFR) unsuitable for most injection.

summary: Algerian recyclers advertise PET/PVC/PEHD/PP broyé and granules, 20 t/week to 1,000 t/month, some exporting
implication: A regrind supply base exists; names need phone verification.

summary: El Kader Plast (Oggaz, Mascara): 2,000 kg/h PP/PEHD recycling line, 70% of granules sold on market, 30% to pallet unit
implication: Candidate supplier of recycled PP/HDPE for non-cosmetic parts (pallet feet, spacers).

summary: Kompass Algeria lists only ~3 colour-masterbatch makers (Himaplast, Decoplast, BRUM) plus Smart Polymer Colors; Taif Master Batch on dzentreprise
implication: Thin local MB base: get 2 MB sources (1 local, 1 importer) and qualify colour early.

summary: Film converter Plastedj uses Italian reference masterbatches for UV-stabilised agricultural film
implication: UV MB likely imported; ask distributors for UV/HALS MB with outdoor ratings.

summary: UAE Polytec and EuP Egypt market colour/additive MB specifically to Algeria
implication: Import alternative to local MB; Egyptian GAFTA origin less Hormuz-exposed than UAE.

summary: Algeria consumes ~2 bn USD/yr of raw plastic (2019); imports grew 304 kt (2007) to 817 kt (2015); Algeria produces ~3% of its raw-material needs
implication: Structural import dependence; distributors exist in every major region.

summary: Algerian Interior Minister acknowledged a 'fierce' rise in prices (headline only)
implication: General inflation context Oct 2026; plastics not specifically confirmed.

summary: Algerian buyer (Groupe Med Dora) posted request for SABIC polypropylene
implication: SABIC grades are a reference in Algerian buying; Saudi origin = Hormuz/Red Sea exposure (Yanbu Red Sea plants less so).
